**STEP 1 - Scene:** A single portion of scrambled eggs on an otherwise empty plate.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** A white square dinner plate, about 25 cm per side with rounded corners. Since it is square, I used side × side instead of the circle formula: about 600 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Scrambled eggs, probably cooked with a little butter or oil. No sauce or other food is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The eggs form an irregular mound in the upper-right corner, covering about 9% of the plate. That is the only food, so total coverage is about 9%, or about 54 cm².

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The mound is about 2.5 cm high on average, giving 54 cm² × 2.5 cm ≈ 135 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Scrambled curds are dense but have some gaps, so I used a bulk density of 0.8 g/ml. That gives 135 ml × 0.8 ≈ 108 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Scrambled eggs with a little fat are about 150 kcal per 100 g. 108 g × 1.5 ≈ 162 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** About 108 g is roughly two eggs scrambled, which fits this modest pile. The estimate is plausible.
